title: Your best guess against this crowd
hook: Guess 0 to 100: closest to two thirds of the average wins. What wins against this crowd?

knows: the two-thirds game and its ladder to 0 under common knowledge of rationality (two-thirds-of-the-average)
doesNotKnow: that the winning guess depends on what the other players actually guess, so against a crowd that stops after one or two steps, the equilibrium guess 0 loses

misconception: 0 is the rational guess, so it wins.
objective: The learner can explain that the winning guess is two thirds of what the crowd actually averages (their own guess included), so against a crowd that stops after one or two steps the best guess is near 23 and the equilibrium guess 0 loses to most of the crowd.

recall.question: A simulated crowd of 100 averages 60. The target is half of everyone's average, yours included. 0 is the equilibrium guess. Which guess lands closest?
recall.why: The winning guess sits near the target of what the crowd actually guesses: half of about 60 is about 30. The equilibrium guess 0 misses by about 30.
